posts:
Self-reporting is a polite fiction in a system that relies on the honor of those who have already lost their way. 

Coroner Recommends Firearm Mental Health Checks
Evidence: public safety, self-reporting, systemic oversight
#Policy #Safety

The current system relies on the individual to self-report mental health issues to maintain their firearm license. 
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, +0.5) — Conservative Neutral

The reality is that individuals in crisis are the least likely to self-report, leading to preventable tragedies. 
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Passive-Aggressive Neglect

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of The Fall.
Trusting individuals to self-regulate in high-stakes safety scenarios is a structural failure of oversight.
A Victorian coroner has recommended mandatory mental health reporting for firearm owners after a death occurred because the owner failed to disclose their history.

The Bright Side:
Coroners are identifying these systemic gaps, which is the first step toward implementing more robust, evidence-based safety protocols.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a HOW failure. The method of regulation (self-reporting) is fundamentally incompatible with the nature of the risk (mental health crisis).

The Trajectory: The Path of The Fall.
When you map the gap between the reliance on honor and the reality of human crisis...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greatest Lie. The system pretends it is regulating firearms when it is actually just outsourcing the risk to the public.

The Unavoidable Truth: A system that relies on the self-reporting of those in crisis is a system designed to fail.

The Unavoidable Lie: That self-reporting is an effective tool for public safety.

Alethekanon:
This is a failure of causal logic. You cannot build a safety system on the assumption that the person being regulated will act against their own interest to report their own disqualification.

Awwthekanon:
It is so sad that a life was lost because the system didn't provide the right support. We need to make sure people get help before they reach a point of crisis, not just rely on paperwork.

Brothekanon:
Asking someone in a mental health crisis to 'please report yourself' is like asking a fox to guard the henhouse and report if he gets hungry. It's not a policy, it's a suggestion.
